subproblem.title: The functional β ↦ ζ(β∧α) is represented by V = Σ_l ζ(e_l♭∧α)e_l, and V ∈ Q when ζ orients Q
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let ζ ∈ Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P (n+1) (a continuous linear functional on (n+1)-covectors) and let α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n. For a 1-covector β : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ write β∧α := alternatizeUncurryFin(β.smulRight α), so that (β∧α)(v_0, …, v_n) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i·β(v_i)·α(v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_n). Let e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin P) be the standard basis, e_l♭ := innerSL ℝ e_l = ⟨e_l, ·⟩, and V := Σ_l ζ(e_l♭∧α)·e_l ∈ ℝ^P. Then (1) ζ(β∧α) = β(V) for every 1-covector β; and (2) V ∈ Q for every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P of which ζ is a unit orientation (IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ζ : MultiVector P (n + 1)) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), (∀ β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ, ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight α)) = β (∑ l : Fin P, ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ))).smulRight α)) • EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ))) ∧ ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q → (∑ l : Fin P, ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ))).smulRight α)) • EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ)) ∈ Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4(a) and 4(b) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of Lemma 4.5(2), display (3): ⟨dh∧ω, ξ⟩ = ⟨dh, Ṽ⟩ with Ṽ tangent), stated pointwise for one multivector ζ and one covector α. Notation: Φ(β) := ζ(β∧α) = ζ(alternatizeUncurryFin(β.smulRight α)) for β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ; e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1; e_l♭ := innerSL ℝ e_l, so e_l♭(v) = ⟨e_l, v⟩; V := Σ_{l ∈ Fin P} Φ(e_l♭)·e_l.

1. (Φ is linear.) For β₁, β₂ and c ∈ ℝ: (β₁ + β₂).smulRight α = β₁.smulRight α + β₂.smulRight α and (c•β).smulRight α = c•(β.smulRight α) (check at each vector v: (β₁ v + β₂ v)•α = β₁ v•α + β₂ v•α by `add_smul`, and (c·β v)•α = c•(β v•α) by `mul_smul`). alternatizeUncurryFin is additive and ℝ-homogeneous (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add`, `ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul`) and ζ is linear (`map_add`, `map_smul`). Hence Φ(β₁ + β₂) = Φ(β₁) + Φ(β₂) and Φ(c•β) = c·Φ(β), so Φ is an ℝ-linear map (Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ and commutes with finite sums (`map_sum`).
2. (Expansion of a 1-covector.) For every v ∈ ℝ^P, v = Σ_l v_l·e_l (`(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).sum_repr v`), so β(v) = Σ_l v_l·β(e_l) by linearity of β; and e_l♭(v) = ⟨e_l, v⟩ = v_l (`innerSL_apply_apply`, `EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left`). Hence β = Σ_l β(e_l)•e_l♭ as continuous linear functionals (ext at every v).
3. (Identity (1).) By steps 1 and 2, Φ(β) = Φ(Σ_l β(e_l)•e_l♭) = Σ_l β(e_l)·Φ(e_l♭). By linearity of β, β(V) = Σ_l Φ(e_l♭)·β(e_l). The two finite sums agree term by term (commutativity), so ζ(β∧α) = Φ(β) = β(V) for every β.
4. (Normal directions are annihilated.) Let ζ be a unit orientation of Q: there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_0, …, τ_n) with span(range τ) = Q such that ζ(γ) = γ(τ) for all (n+1)-covectors γ, or ζ(γ) = −γ(τ) for all γ. Let v ∈ Q^⊥. Each τ_i lies in span(range τ) = Q (`Submodule.subset_span`), so ⟨v, τ_i⟩ = 0 (`Submodule.inner_left_of_mem_orthogonal`). By `ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply`, (v♭∧α)(τ) = Σ_i (−1)^i·((v♭.smulRight α)(τ_i))(τ with τ_i removed) = Σ_i (−1)^i·⟨v, τ_i⟩·α(τ with τ_i removed) = 0, every summand vanishing. Hence Φ(v♭) = ζ(v♭∧α) = ±0 = 0 in either sign case.
5. (Membership (2).) For every v ∈ Q^⊥, ⟨v, V⟩ = v♭(V) = Φ(v♭) = 0 by identity (1) with β := v♭ and step 4. So V ∈ (Q^⊥)^⊥ (`Submodule.mem_orthogonal`). Q is a subspace of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, hence complete, so it has an orthogonal projection and Q^⊥⊥ = Q (`Submodule.orthogonal_orthogonal`; the instance is found automatically). Therefore V ∈ Q. ∎

theorem Submission.dor_lmbsf_ll_wedge_representing_vector : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ζ : MultiVector P (n + 1)) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), (∀ β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ, ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight α)) = β (∑ l : Fin P, ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ))).smulRight α)) • EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ))) ∧ ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q → (∑ l : Fin P, ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ))).smulRight α)) • EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ)) ∈ Q := by
  intro P n ζ α
  -- Φ(β) := ζ(β ∧ α) is linear in β
  let Φ : (Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) → ℝ := fun β =>
    ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight α))
  have hΦadd : ∀ β₁ β₂ : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ, Φ (β₁ + β₂) = Φ β₁ + Φ β₂ := by
    intro β₁ β₂
    have : (β₁ + β₂).smulRight α = β₁.smulRight α + β₂.smulRight α := by
      ext v; simp [add_smul]
    simp only [Φ, this, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add, map_add]
  have hΦsmul : ∀ (c : ℝ) (β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ), Φ (c • β) = c • Φ β := by
    intro c β
    have : (c • β).smulRight α = c • β.smulRight α := by
      ext v; simp [mul_smul]
    simp only [Φ, this, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul, map_smul]
  let Φl : (Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ :=
    { toFun := Φ, map_add' := hΦadd, map_smul' := hΦsmul }
  -- expansion of a covector in the standard dual basis
  have hβexp : ∀ β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ,
      β = ∑ l : Fin P, β (EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ)) • innerSL ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ)) := by
    intro β
    ext v
    have hv : v = ∑ l : Fin P, v l • EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ) := by
      conv_lhs => rw [← (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).sum_repr v]
      simp
    simp only [FunLike.coe_sum, Finset.sum_apply, FunLike.coe_smul,
      Pi.smul_apply, innerSL_apply_apply, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left, map_one, one_mul,
      smul_eq_mul]
    conv_lhs => rw [hv]
    simp [map_sum, map_smul, mul_comm]
  have hid : ∀ β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ, Φ β = β (∑ l : Fin P, Φ (innerSL ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ))) •
      EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ)) := by
    intro β
    have h1 : Φ β = Φl β := rfl
    rw [h1, hβexp β, map_sum]
    simp only [map_sum, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro l _
    simp only [Φl, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk]
    have := hβexp β
    rw [← this]
    ring
  refine ⟨hid, ?_⟩
  intro Q hQ
  obtain ⟨τ, hτ, hspan, hsign⟩ := hQ
  have hzero : ∀ v ∈ Qᗮ, Φ (innerSL ℝ v) = 0 := by
    intro v hv
    have hτQ : ∀ i, τ i ∈ Q := fun i => hspan ▸ Submodule.subset_span (Set.mem_range_self i)
    have hval : (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α)) τ = 0 := by
      rw [ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply]
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro i _
      simp [Submodule.inner_left_of_mem_orthogonal (hτQ i) hv]
    rcases hsign with h | h
    · simp only [Φ, h, hval]
    · simp only [Φ, h, hval, neg_zero]
  rw [← Submodule.orthogonal_orthogonal Q, Submodule.mem_orthogonal]
  intro u hu
  have := hid (innerSL ℝ u)
  rw [hzero u hu, innerSL_apply_apply] at this
  exact this.symm
```
proof_key_steps: Φ(β) := ζ(β∧α) is ℝ-linear in β (smulRight, alternatizeUncurryFin and ζ are linear).
β = Σ_l β(e_l)e_l♭, so Φ(β) = Σ_l β(e_l)Φ(e_l♭) = β(V).
If ζ = ±(·)(τ) with τ an orthonormal basis of Q and v ⊥ Q, then (v♭∧α)(τ) = Σ_i (−1)^i⟨v, τ_i⟩α(…) = 0, so Φ(v♭) = 0.
⟨v, V⟩ = Φ(v♭) = 0 for all v ∈ Q^⊥, hence V ∈ Q^⊥⊥ = Q.

subproblem.title: Dominated convergence for the action of an integer multiplicity triple under bounded pointwise-convergent multipliers
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U of dimension n (IMRep U n, with M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient), and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n). Let h_k : ℝ^P → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) be Borel measurable, let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be any function, and let C ∈ ℝ be such that |h_k(x)| ≤ C for all k and x and h_k(x) → h(x) as k → ∞ for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then, with Hⁿ = μHE[n] and Bochner integrals, ∫_M θ(x)·h_k(x)·⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) → ∫_M θ(x)·h(x)·⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) as k → ∞, where ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = R.orient x (ω x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (hs : ℕ → Euclid P → ℝ) (h : Euclid P → ℝ) (C : ℝ), (∀ k, Measurable (hs k)) → (∀ k x, |hs k x| ≤ C) → (∀ x, Tendsto (fun k => hs k x) atTop (𝓝 (h x))) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * hs k x * R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * h x * R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the two outer terms of identity (i) converge by dominated convergence), stated once for an arbitrary integer multiplicity triple and test form so that it applies both to (RB, ω) and to (RT, dω). Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict R.carrier; G(x) := θ(x)·⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (ω x), where ω also denotes the underlying form (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n).

1. (Integrable kernel.) By the sibling action_integrable (Lean `Submission.rsd_cmr_ic_action_integrable P n U R ω`), G is μ-integrable.
2. (Rewriting the integrands.) For every x, θ(x)·h_k(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = h_k(x)·G(x) and θ(x)·h(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = h(x)·G(x), by commutativity and associativity of multiplication in ℝ (`funext` and `ring`). So it suffices to prove ∫ h_k·G dμ → ∫ h·G dμ.
3. (Measurability.) h_k is measurable and real-valued, hence a.e. strongly measurable (`Measurable.aestronglyMeasurable`); G is integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable. So F_k := h_k·G is a.e. strongly measurable for μ (`AEStronglyMeasurable.mul`).
4. (Domination.) For every k and x, ‖F_k(x)‖ = |h_k(x)|·‖G(x)‖ ≤ C·‖G(x)‖ (`norm_mul`, the hypothesis |h_k(x)| ≤ C and ‖G(x)‖ ≥ 0, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right`). The bound x ↦ C·‖G(x)‖ is μ-integrable (`Integrable.norm`, `Integrable.const_mul`).
5. (Pointwise convergence.) For every x, h_k(x)·G(x) → h(x)·G(x) as k → ∞ (`Tendsto.mul_const` applied to the hypothesis h_k(x) → h(x)).
6. (Dominated convergence.) By steps 3–5 and `tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence`, ∫ h_k·G dμ → ∫ h·G dμ. By step 2 this is the claim ∫_M θ·h_k·⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ → ∫_M θ·h·⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ. ∎

theorem Submission.dor_lmbsf_ll_action_mul_tendsto : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (hs : ℕ → Euclid P → ℝ) (h : Euclid P → ℝ) (C : ℝ), (∀ k, Measurable (hs k)) → (∀ k x, |hs k x| ≤ C) → (∀ x, Tendsto (fun k => hs k x) atTop (𝓝 (h x))) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * hs k x * R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * h x * R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n])) := by
  intro P n U R ω hs h C hmeas hbdd hlim
  have hG := Submission.rsd_cmr_ic_action_integrable P n U R ω
  set G : Euclid P → ℝ := fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x)
    with hG_def
  have key : ∀ k, (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * hs k x * R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x))
      = fun x => hs k x * G x := by
    intro k; funext x; simp only [G]; ring
  have keyh : (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * h x * R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x))
      = fun x => h x * G x := by
    funext x; simp only [G]; ring
  rw [keyh]
  simp_rw [key]
  refine tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence (fun x => C * ‖G x‖) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro k; exact (hmeas k).aestronglyMeasurable.mul hG.aestronglyMeasurable
  · exact hG.norm.const_mul C
  · intro k
    filter_upwards with x
    rw [norm_mul]
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hbdd k x) (norm_nonneg _)
  · filter_upwards with x
    exact (hlim x).mul_const (G x)
```
proof_key_steps: G := θξ(ω) is integrable on M (sibling action_integrable).
Rewrite θ·h_k·ξ(ω) = h_k·G and θ·h·ξ(ω) = h·G.
h_k·G is a.e. strongly measurable, dominated by C|G| (integrable), and converges pointwise to h·G.

subproblem.title: Smooth approximants of the Lipschitz cut-off γ_{a,b}∘f with bounded gradients, converging uniformly
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz (L ≥ 0, LipschitzWith L f) and let a < b be real. Put h(x) := γ_{a,b}(f(x)) = min{1, max{0, (b − f(x))/(b − a)}}. Then there exist functions h_k : ℝ^P → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) and a real constant c such that: every h_k is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (h_k)); ‖Dh_k(x)‖ ≤ c for all k and x (operator norm of fderiv ℝ (h_k) x); |h_k(x)| ≤ 2 for all k and x; and h_k → h uniformly on ℝ^P as k → ∞ (TendstoUniformly along atTop).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (a b : ℝ), LipschitzWith L f → a < b → ∃ (hs : ℕ → Euclid P → ℝ) (c : ℝ), (∀ k, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (hs k)) ∧ (∀ k x, ‖fderiv ℝ (hs k) x‖ ≤ c) ∧ (∀ k x, |hs k x| ≤ 2) ∧ TendstoUniformly hs (fun x => min 1 (max 0 ((b - f x) / (b - a)))) atTop
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (mollified cut-offs h_k of h = γ_{a,b}∘f), with the mollification supplied by the sibling lipschitz_smoothing (Lean Submission.cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing: for a K-Lipschitz g : ℝ^P → ℝ and σ > 0 there is a C^∞ function g' with ‖Dg'(x)‖ ≤ K and |g'(x) − g(x)| ≤ K·σ for every x). Instead of the parent's scales δ_k = 1/(k+1) we use σ_k = 1/((K+1)(k+1)), which also gives the uniform bound |h_k| ≤ 2.

Notation: δ := b − a > 0; γ(s) := min{1, max{0, (b − s)/δ}} for s ∈ ℝ; h := γ∘f, i.e. h(x) = min{1, max{0, (b − f(x))/δ}}; K := (1/δ)·L ≥ 0 (in Lean the NNReal `Real.toNNReal (b - a)⁻¹ * L`, whose coercion to ℝ is (b − a)⁻¹·L).

subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U of dimension n+1 (IMRep U (n+1), with M = R.carrier and ξ = R.orient), let ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) be a continuous n-form (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n), and let B ∈ ℝ satisfy ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. Then there exist a Borel measurable W : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and c′ ∈ ℝ such that: W(x) = 0 whenever ω(x) = 0; ‖W(x)‖ ≤ c′ for all x; and for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ M (μHE[n+1].restrict M; one null set for all β), W(x) ∈ T_xM := approxTangentPlane (n+1) M x and, for every 1-covector β : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ, ξ(x)(β∧ω(x)) = β(W(x)), where β∧ω(x) := alternatizeUncurryFin(β.smulRight ω(x)).

MultiVector P (n+1) carries the operator norm, so |L(γ)| ≤ ‖L‖‖γ‖ (`ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm`).

1. (Strongly measurable version of ξ.) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ (field `R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient`). Let ξ₁ := `R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient.mk R.orient`; then ξ₁ is strongly measurable (`AEStronglyMeasurable.stronglyMeasurable_mk`) and ξ = ξ₁ μ-a.e. (`AEStronglyMeasurable.ae_eq_mk`).
2. (Truncation.) S := {x : ‖ξ₁(x)‖ ≤ 1} is measurable, since x ↦ ‖ξ₁(x)‖ is strongly measurable real-valued, hence measurable (`StronglyMeasurable.norm`, with the type `β := MultiVector P (n + 1)` given explicitly, then `measurableSet_le`). Let ξ₀ := ξ₁ on S and ξ₀ := 0 off S (`S.piecewise ξ₁ 0`). ξ₀ is strongly measurable (`StronglyMeasurable.piecewise`) and ‖ξ₀(x)‖ ≤ 1 for every x (on S by definition, off S because ‖0‖ = 0).
3. (Coefficient forms.) For l ∈ Fin P put A_l(x) := e_l♭∧ω(x) ∈ Λ^{n+1}. A_l is continuous: x ↦ (e_l♭, ω(x)) is continuous, (β, γ) ↦ β.smulRight γ is a bounded bilinear map (`isBoundedBilinearMap_smulRight`), and alternatizeUncurryFin is a continuous linear map (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM`, `alternatizeUncurryFinCLM_apply`). Hence A_l is strongly measurable (`Continuous.stronglyMeasurable`; ℝ^P is second countable), the pair x ↦ (ξ₀(x), A_l(x)) is strongly measurable (`StronglyMeasurable.prodMk`), and since evaluation (L, γ) ↦ L(γ) is continuous (`isBoundedBilinearMap_apply`), c_l(x) := ξ₀(x)(A_l(x)) is strongly measurable (`Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable`), hence measurable.
4. (The field.) Define W(x) := Σ_{l ∈ Fin P} c_l(x)·e_l. W is Borel measurable as a finite sum of measurable real functions times constant vectors (`Finset.measurable_sum`, `Measurable.smul_const`).
5. (Vanishing.) If ω(x) = 0 then e_l♭.smulRight 0 = 0 and alternatizeUncurryFin 0 = 0 (evaluate with `alternatizeUncurryFin_apply`), so A_l(x) = 0, c_l(x) = ξ₀(x)(0) = 0 for every l, and W(x) = 0.
6. (Bound.) For all l and x: ‖A_l(x)‖ ≤ (n + 1)·‖e_l♭.smulRight ω(x)‖ (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_alternatizeUncurryFin_le`) = (n + 1)·‖e_l♭‖·‖ω(x)‖ (`ContinuousLinearMap.norm_smulRight_apply`) = (n + 1)·‖ω(x)‖ (‖e_l♭‖ = ‖e_l‖ = 1 by `innerSL_apply_norm` and the norm of `EuclideanSpace.single`) ≤ (n + 1)·B. Hence |c_l(x)| ≤ ‖ξ₀(x)‖·‖A_l(x)‖ ≤ (n + 1)·B, and ‖W(x)‖ ≤ Σ_l |c_l(x)|·‖e_l‖ ≤ P·(n + 1)·B =: c' (`norm_sum_le`, `norm_smul`).
7. (Almost-everywhere identification.) By the sibling orient_tangent (Lean `Submission.fvmb_imrep_ae_unitOrientation_approxTangentPlane P (n + 1) U R`), for μ-a.e. x, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM := approxTangentPlane (n + 1) M x. Intersect this full-measure set with {ξ = ξ₁} (step 1) and fix x in the intersection. By the sibling orient_norm (Lean `Submission.unit_orientation_norm_le_one`), ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1, so ‖ξ₁(x)‖ = ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1, x ∈ S, and ξ₀(x) = ξ₁(x) = ξ(x). Therefore W(x) = Σ_l ξ(x)(e_l♭∧ω(x))·e_l, which is exactly the vector V of the sibling wedge_vector (Lean `Submission.dor_lmbsf_ll_wedge_representing_vector P n (R.orient x) (ω x)`) for ζ := ξ(x) and α := ω(x). Part (1) of that sibling gives ξ(x)(β∧ω(x)) = β(W(x)) for every 1-covector β, and part (2) with Q := T_xM gives W(x) ∈ T_xM.
8. (Conclusion.) W and c' satisfy all four requirements: W is Borel measurable (step 4), W(x) = 0 whenever ω(x) = 0 (step 5), ‖W(x)‖ ≤ c' for all x (step 6), and for μ-a.e. x, W(x) ∈ T_xM and ξ(x)(β∧ω(x)) = β(W(x)) for all β (step 7). ∎
